analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: The page covers how a bill becomes a law in 7 steps from introduction through committee chamber votes and presidential action and how House and Senate lawmaking powers differ

overview.headline: Congress turns bill ideas into law through 7 ordered steps

keyPoints.point: Congress serves as the lawmaking branch of the federal government
keyPoints.quote: Congress is the lawmaking branch of the federal government.

keyPoints.point: A bill is a proposal for a new law or a change to existing law brought by members or petitions
keyPoints.quote: A bill is a proposal for a new law or a change to an existing law.

keyPoints.point: Once introduced a bill is assigned to a committee whose members research discuss and make changes
keyPoints.quote: Once a bill is introduced, it is assigned to a committee whose members will research, discuss, and make changes to the bill.

keyPoints.point: Both bodies must vote to accept the same version of the bill before presenting it to the president
keyPoints.quote: Once both bodies vote to accept a bill, they must work out any differences between the two versions.

keyPoints.point: If the president vetoes a bill Congress can often vote to override that veto and make it law
keyPoints.quote: If the president chooses to veto a bill, in most cases Congress can vote to override that veto and the bill becomes a law.

keyTerms.gloss: a proposal for a new law or a change to existing law
keyTerms.quote: A bill is a proposal for a new law or a change to an existing law.

keyTerms.gloss: group assigned to research discuss and make changes to a bill
keyTerms.quote: Once a bill is introduced, it is assigned to a committee whose members will research, discuss, and make changes to the bill.

keyTerms.gloss: refuse to approve a bill by the president called a veto
keyTerms.quote: Or the president can refuse to approve a bill. This is called a veto.

keyTerms.gloss: action where an unsigned bill is vetoed by default when Congress is no longer in session and cannot be overridden
keyTerms.quote: This action is called a pocket veto, and it cannot be overridden by Congress.

keyTerms.gloss: chamber that can initiate tax and revenue related legislation
keyTerms.quote: Only the House can initiate tax and revenue-related legislation

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: The page lists 7 numbered steps from idea to presidential action which is ideal for ordered recall in teaching order
componentPlan.focusQuote: Once a bill is introduced, it is assigned to a committee whose members will research, discuss, and make changes to the bill.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: House and Senate differences are presented as parallel rules that benefit from side by side comparison
componentPlan.focusQuote: Only the House can initiate tax and revenue-related legislation
